industry.why: Overweight, carried; the row's written condition for Double Overweight fired on its letter (relative strength B, 27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; defensives leading cyclicals at one week +1.9, four weeks +4.8 and three months +9.5 points) and is declined, said plainly: the Consumer staples Industry Memo (26-Nov-26) reads the tailwind as supportive and moderate at three months and neutral by twelve, staples lagged on all three rebound days of the week and were the only industry down on 27-Nov, and Goldman Sachs (Jaisson, 20-Nov) calls the 14% defensive rotation mature; see component 1, Special topics, Topics 2, 4 and 5. The 27-Nov-26 regime (risk-off in the open, defensives leading on all five windows) is the reason for B. Three live holdings here (Carlsberg 4.50%, Fevertree 2.40%, Hilton Food 4.70%). Counter-case: declining a written condition twice is goalpost-moving, and Richard may prefer the rule. To A only if the three-month defensives line holds above +2 points and the Industry Memo's twelve-month verdict turns supportive; to C if the three-month line falls under +2.

sector.why: Overweight, carried: non-discretionary demand and proven cases, with the staples industry. Relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; D prior), the one staples sector the market has not paid for. One live holding, Hilton Food (4.70%), whose tight-line tranche exited on an up day this week (component 1, Topic 2). Counter-case: input-cost inflation squeezes producers before retailers, and the tape says the market agrees. Holds B with the industry; to C if the industry goes to C.

geography.why: Overweight, from Neutral, on the row's own written condition ('to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read'): Goldman's Sharon Bell (20-Nov) argues 'Domestic not Defensive' with 2027 growth of 1.4% above consensus and the FTSE 100 at a discount with a far higher free-cash-flow yield, James Moberly (23-Nov) has growth improving through 2027 as rates peak, Marshall (22-Nov) has gilts at 4.8% by end-2027, UK core inflation is flat at 2.8% (25-Nov), and Jefferies' Duncan Farr (26-Nov) reads the Financial Policy Committee ruling as favourable for bank cost of equity. 28 Pool stocks are UK-listed and now carry a country weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum; the book holds 16.47 points UK-listed (CVS Group, Fevertree, Hilton Food, Helios Towers). Counter-case: Bell's next two quarters are 'tough', the Bank of England's decision is still unread, Oppenheimer underweights Europe as a whole, and the UK Pool names are mostly global businesses. Back to C if the Bank of England's guidance is read hawkish or a UK consumer reading arrives falling.
